title: Console: switch cost breakdown aggregation to Cost Model API (flagged + fallback + metrics)
author: Chloe Martin
description: Problem: Console cost breakdown pages currently rely on legacy aggregation logic (token metering + heuristics) that can diverge from billing hooks and Optimize. This PR updates Console backend aggregation to call the internal Cost Model API v1 for per-request and aggregated breakdowns, behind a feature flag, with explicit fail-open fallback to the legacy path to protect the Console hot path. Scope: (1) New CostModelClient wiring in console-backend using the shared client library (timeouts/retries/version negotiation), (2) route-level and org-level breakdown queries now source canonical taxonomy from the cost-model service (prefill/decode, cache hits, batch efficiency, overhead allocation), (3) feature flag + gradual rollout controls, (4) metrics/tracing so we can compare legacy vs cost-model output and watch latency/error budgets. Flagging/rollout: gated by `console.cost_breakdown.use_cost_model_api` (default off), with per-tenant allowlist support for staged enablement; fallback behavior is fail-open to legacy if the cost-model call times out (>250ms), returns 4xx schema/version errors, or is in a circuit-open state due to elevated 5xx. API usage: uses `CostModelAPI.BreakdownV1` endpoint with bounded dimensions (max 20 routes, max 10 models, max 50 groups total) and requests `schema_version=1.x` (accepts unknown fields). Determinism: request includes explicit `window_start`, `window_end`, `deployment_mode`, and `model_version_pins` when present; we propagate Console’s notion of request filters (project, environment, region) into the cost-model query. Observability added: (a) `console.cost_model_api.request_count{status,endpoint}` (b) `console.cost_model_api.latency_ms{endpoint}` (c) `console.cost_model_api.fallback_count{reason}` (d) `console.cost_breakdown.source_count{source=legacy|cost_model}` (e) `console.cost_breakdown.delta_ratio` (sampled) to track drift between the two sources during rollout; spans: `console.costBreakdown.fetch` with child span `costModelAPI.breakdown`. Testing: unit tests with golden fixtures (mocked cost-model responses + legacy output), contract tests around bounding/parameter validation, and a staging smoke test script for the cost breakdown endpoints. Notes: This PR does not change invoices/billing; it only changes the data source for Console views when the flag is enabled. Follow-ups: remove legacy codepath after 100% rollout + drift SLI acceptance; expand breakdown to include optional what-if projections once Console UX is ready.
implementation_notes: Key choices: (1) Timeout 250ms end-to-end for cost-model calls on Console endpoints; `max_attempts=2` with jittered backoff on retryable 5xx only. (2) Circuit breaker: if 5xx rate > 5% over 1m for cost-model calls, open for 30s; while open, always use legacy path and emit `fallback_count{reason=circuit_open}`. (3) Bounding: we cap group cardinality in Console before calling cost-model to avoid accidental unbounded queries from UI filters; we also request `include_debug=false` to keep payload sizes stable. (4) Mapping: legacy fields are mapped onto the standard taxonomy for UI compatibility; we intentionally keep the UI response shape stable and add a `source` field for internal diagnostics only (not exposed to customers). (5) Security/tenancy: tenant/org/project identifiers are taken from existing auth context and passed as service-to-service auth via internal identity; no user PII is included in cost-model requests.

review_conversation: Jada Williams: Can we confirm the UI response shape doesn’t change when the flag is on? Concerned about breaking the dashboard table render if some buckets come back empty. Also, what’s the behavior if cost-model returns only prefill/decode but not overhead?

Chloe Martin (author): Response shape is unchanged; we still return the same `breakdown_rows` array and `totals` object. Missing buckets are filled with zeros server-side. Overhead is optional in v1; if absent we emit `overhead_usd=0` and add `fallback_count{reason=missing_bucket}` only in internal metrics (no UI impact). Added test coverage in `cost_model_mapping.test.ts`.

Ethan Park: Please use the shared client library defaults for version negotiation; we should avoid hard-failing on unknown fields. Also, can we tighten request bounding? I see 50 groups total; that’s okay but the UI filters could produce more if not pre-aggregated.

Chloe Martin (author): Updated to use the client lib `negotiateSchemaVersion('1.*')` and set `ignore_unknown_fields=true`. Also added a pre-aggregation step to cap to top-K routes/models by token volume before calling cost-model; anything outside the cap is rolled into an `other` bucket (consistent with existing UI behavior).

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Tenancy/auth: are we passing tenant id from user input anywhere? Need to ensure this is derived from verified auth context only. Also, confirm the service-to-service principal has least privilege for cost-model endpoints.

Chloe Martin (author): Tenant/org/project IDs are pulled from the existing Console auth middleware (validated JWT + RBAC) and not from query params. Service-to-service uses the existing `console-backend` internal identity with `cost-model:breakdown:read` scope only. Added an explicit deny on any cross-tenant override headers.
Nadia Rahman: For the sampled delta metric, are we comparing the same window and same token accounting? Telemetry lag can make this noisy and trigger false alerts if we later hook it up.

Chloe Martin (author): Delta metric is informational only (dashboard), sampled at 1% and tagged with `telemetry_lag_seconds` from the cost-model response when present. Not wiring alerts off it here; drift SLI/alerting is tracked separately under ENG-4827.

Rafael Mendes: SRE ask: confirm fail-open works even when cost-model is slow but not erroring; timeouts should trip fallback quickly. Also add a metric for circuit breaker open state so we can correlate with incidents (SUP-31905).

Chloe Martin (author): Added hard deadline at 250ms; if exceeded we cancel and fallback. Added `console.cost_model_api.circuit_open_gauge` and `fallback_count{reason=timeout}`. Also added log sampling to avoid spamming on timeout storms.
Allison Grant: Metrics naming looks good. Please ensure we don’t emit high-cardinality labels (route ids, model names) on the hot path. I saw a draft metric with `route` label in an earlier commit.
Chloe Martin (author): Removed route/model labels from counters; only using coarse labels (`endpoint`, `status`, `reason`, `source`). Route/model details are in traces only (sampled), not metrics.
Jada Williams: Approving pending the last push; can you add a short rollout note to the PR description about initial allowlist and rollback plan?
Chloe Martin (author): Added rollout steps + rollback note; flag defaults off, enable for internal orgs first, monitor p95 latency + fallback rate, then expand allowlist.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy with flag OFF globally. 2) Enable `console.cost_breakdown.use_cost_model_api` for Redwood internal orgs + 2 pilot tenants from Marissa’s list. 3) Monitor: p95 cost breakdown endpoint latency, `fallback_count` rate, cost-model 5xx, and sampled delta ratio dashboard. 4) Expand allowlist in 3 waves (25% / 50% / 100%) with a minimum 24h soak between waves. 5) Rollback: disable flag globally (instant) if fallback rate > 10% sustained 10m or if Console p95 regresses > 100ms.
risk_assessment: Main risks are added latency on Console breakdown endpoints and schema/semantics mismatches causing confusing UI output. Mitigations: strict timeout + fail-open fallback, bounded requests, stable response shape, and added metrics/tracing to detect regressions quickly.
release_notes: Internal: Console cost breakdown can now source data from the Standard Cost Model API (behind feature flag) with safe fallback to legacy aggregation.
